input.content: Idempotent save/dedup lookup keyed on the wrong field → silent data loss. In an operation that persists per-key state with retry recovery, changing the existing-record lookup from the idempotency key (operation_id) to a coarser field (workspace) makes any genuinely new operation on an already-seen key resolve to the FIRST stored record. Consequences: (1) new values are never applied (apply() is gated on status=="pending" and the found record is already applied/completed), (2) the new operation_id is never inserted into the recovery map, (3) the function still returns {"ok": True, operation_id} — so the caller is told the write succeeded while it was silently dropped. Tests passed because all cases reused the same workspace+operation_id+values; the bug lives in the untested "second distinct operation on the same workspace" path. Review check: when reviewing dedup/idempotency code, verify the lookup field matches the map's actual key and that a found record still applies updated inputs; and that re-running the terminal step (e.g. receipt) on an already-completed record can't resurface a transient failure that the completed-state short-circuit previously avoided.
